nodes.label: Noise floor
nodes.blurb: The level of background noise in a system when no signal is present

nodes.label: Decibel (dB)
nodes.blurb: Logarithmic unit expressing a ratio between two values

nodes.label: Logarithmic scale
nodes.blurb: dB values are not evenly spaced; the scale compresses large ranges into manageable numbers

nodes.label: Digital headroom
nodes.blurb: Space between the signal level and 0 dBFS

nodes.label: In the DAW
nodes.blurb: Keep individual track levels below 0 dBFS; use channel faders to balance; leave headroom on the master bus

nodes.label: Analogue clipping
nodes.blurb: Gradual — soft clipping compresses peaks, adding harmonic distortion (sometimes musically desirable)

nodes.label: Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR)
nodes.blurb: The difference in dB between the signal level and the noise floor

nodes.label: dBFS
nodes.blurb: Decibels Full Scale — digital reference where 0 dBFS is maximum

nodes.label: Why logarithmic?
nodes.blurb: Matches human perception of loudness (we perceive equal ratios of intensity as equal changes in loudness)
